sources.claim: Original crypto study compares fixed-weight daily and monthly rebalancing with buy-and-hold and attributes the premium to no asset consistently outperforming.
Adversarial prior: optimal rebalance frequency is not universal and depends materially on autocorrelation and expected-return dispersion.
Official public candle endpoint; time is bucket start, one-day granularity is 86400 seconds, responses are capped at 300 and may omit no-tick intervals.

provider.timestamp_semantics: UTC bucket start; use each bucket open as the first trade of that UTC day

data.selection_rule: fixed currently available non-stablecoin USD spot products chosen before outcomes; no additions, removals, substitutions or listing-date optimization
data.missing_bucket_rule: fail unless every UTC date in the closed window has one common daily open for every product

portfolio.strategy: reset to 20 percent per product at the first UTC daily open of each calendar month, then let weights drift
portfolio.benchmark: 20 percent per product at the first window open, then buy and hold with drifting weights
portfolio.initial_purchase_cost: same initial allocation on both sleeves and excluded from active difference
portfolio.turnover: one_way half-L1 distance from pre-rebalance drifting weights to equal weights

costs.application: charge strategy rebalance turnover only; buy-and-hold has no post-initial trades

trial_accounting.selection_rule: no universe, frequency, dates, costs, folds, seed, missing-data rule or gate changes after any product candle byte
